$comment: The canonical TypeScript, ESLint, Prettier and knip settings for an Expo app (single app at the repo root; verified 2026-10-03 with TypeScript 6.0.3, ESLint 9.39.5, typescript-eslint 8.70.1, Prettier 3.9.9, knip 6.38.0). check-configs.mjs compares the app repo against this file. {srcDir} is the resolved source folder. Change it only together with the templates; a change is a stop-and-ask decision and lands with a Gate-Change trailer.

programs.world: Node and tests: the whole repo with Node types

excludeWhy.{srcDir}/app-env.d.ts: the app program's declare const process would replace @types/node's process in the root program (TS2339 on process.exitCode)
excludeWhy.skills: installed skills hold templates and planted-bug fixtures that belong to no program

programs.world: app: the bundled code, no Node types

includeWhy.{toRoot}.expo/types/**/*.ts: Expo Router's typed routes are a global augmentation nothing imports; without the include the app program types every href as a plain string

programs.excludeWhy: excluding a folder from the app program drops the no-Node-types guarantee for it while the root program still checks it with Node types

required.what: linterOptions.noInlineConfig: true (inline eslint-disable comments do nothing)
eslint-config-prettier as the LAST entry of defineConfig([...])
no-floating-promises with ignoreVoid: false and ignoreIIFE: false
strict-boolean-expressions with allowString: false and allowNumber: false
no-unused-vars with args: 'all' and caughtErrors: 'all' (ESLint, not tsc, owns unused code)
the enums selector, verbatim (TSEnumDeclaration in no-restricted-syntax)
the NODE_IMPORT_EXTENSION selector, verbatim (Node-run files write ./x.ts)
the IS_MULTI_PACKAGE switch that adds PACKAGE_IMPORT_EXTENSION to runtimeSyntax()
the NODE_BUILTINS pattern (no Node built-ins in app code)
restrictedImports() prepending BANNED_PACKAGE_PATHS to every no-restricted-imports list
VENDOR_SDK_PATHS spread into RUNTIME_PATHS (a vendor SDK is imported only by its adapter)
the react-native-google-mobile-ads adapter-only ban in VENDOR_SDK_PATHS (AdsPort/ConsentPort)
the expo-iap adapter-only ban in VENDOR_SDK_PATHS (PurchasePort)
the expo-sqlite adapter-only ban in VENDOR_SDK_PATHS (SqlDriver)
ATT_IMPORT in BANNED_PACKAGE_PATHS, so every file but the consent adapter keeps the ban
the axios ban in BANNED_PACKAGE_PATHS (network goes through the ApiClient)
the react-native-iap ban in BANNED_PACKAGE_PATHS (IAP goes through PurchasePort)
the react-native-restart ban in BANNED_PACKAGE_PATHS (reloadAppAsync from expo)
ATT_ADAPTER naming one consent adapter (src/services/consent/*-consent-adapter.ts and its platform files), not a folder of adapters
the ATT_ADAPTER block, the one place allow: [ATT_IMPORT] lifts the ban
the ADAPTERS block (the one place that lifts the vendor SDK bans)
the asyncHandler selector, verbatim (async on* handlers, handleSubmit(...) on an on* prop, async handleX functions)
the handlerBody selector, verbatim (an on* handler or handleX has a block body and returns nothing, so no-floating-promises sees the promise it starts)
the ON_PROP selector part the asyncHandler selector builds on, verbatim
the HANDLER_NAME selector part (handleX variables) the handler selectors build on, verbatim
the setTimeoutNoDelay selector, verbatim (every timer names its delay)
the newDate selector, verbatim (no new Date() in app code)
the remoteUrl selector (remote URLs live in src/api and src/config)
the network globals list (fetch, XMLHttpRequest, WebSocket, EventSource)
the runtime block's no-restricted-globals with NETWORK_GLOBALS (network only through the ApiClient)
the runtime block's no-restricted-properties with RESTRICTED_PROPERTIES

required.pattern: object:\s*'Math',\s*property:\s*'random',\s*message:\s*'Use the seeded RNG \(src/core/rng\) or an injected random source\.'
required.what: the Math.random entry with its canonical message (quality-gates.json compares the resolved entries verbatim)
the Date.now entry with its canonical message 'Inject ClockPort (src/services/clock).'
the performance.now entry with its canonical message
the I18nManager.isRTL entry with its canonical message
the PURE block (src/core imports no React, React Native, Expo or app layers)
the DETERMINISM_SYNTAX list, verbatim (the Math allow-list and the ** ban in deterministic folders)
the localeCompare, Intl and toLocale*Case bans in DETERMINISM_SYNTAX (deterministic code never reads the device locale)
the DETERMINISTIC block with [...runtimeSyntax(), ...DETERMINISM_SYNTAX] (integer-safe math in src/core/rng, src/core/dates and game rules)
the Expo Router block (route files may default-export)
react/jsx-no-literals: error (every visible string comes from the catalogs)
'skills/**' in globalIgnores (installed skills hold templates and planted-bug fixtures)
'.agents/**' in globalIgnores (where npx skills add installs)
the PRE_EXISTING list spread into globalIgnores (top-level folders that are not app code)

maxOccurrences.what: tseslint.configs.disableTypeChecked (allowed only for the plain JS config files)
an allow list that lifts a banned package for a block (the canonical config has one: the consent adapter)
a hand-written no-restricted-imports array (every block uses restrictedImports() or RUNTIME_IMPORTS)
maxOccurrences.fix: Rebuild it from the shared lists: 'no-restricted-imports': restrictedImports({ paths: without(RUNTIME_PATHS, ONE_EXEMPTED_ENTRY), patterns: [NODE_BUILTINS] }); a fresh list drops every vendor, Text, react-intl, memo, Node-built-in and parent-import ban for those files.

maxOccurrences.what: a fresh no-restricted-syntax list (literal entries instead of the shared lists)
maxOccurrences.fix: Rebuild it from the shared lists: runtimeSyntax(['oneSelectorKey']) drops one SYNTAX entry and keeps the rest (asyncHandler, RTL, URL, newDate ...).

maxOccurrences.what: a fresh no-restricted-properties list (literal entries instead of the shared lists)
maxOccurrences.fix: Rebuild it from the shared lists: ['error', ...withoutProperty('Date', 'now')] (or PERF_PROPERTIES) keeps every other banned property.

maxOccurrences.what: a fresh no-restricted-globals list (literal entries instead of the shared lists)
maxOccurrences.fix: Rebuild it from the shared lists: ['error', ...TEST_GLOBALS] or ['error', ...NETWORK_GLOBALS, ...TEST_GLOBALS] keeps every other banned global.

maxOccurrences.what: restrictedImports({}) (the package bans only; the canonical config uses it for block 4 and for __mocks__/jest.setup.ts)
maxOccurrences.fix: Start from the runtime lists: 'no-restricted-imports': RUNTIME_IMPORTS, or restrictedImports({ paths: without(RUNTIME_PATHS, ONE_EXEMPTED_ENTRY), patterns: [NODE_BUILTINS] }); restrictedImports({}) drops every vendor, Text, react-intl, memo and Node-built-in ban for its files.

maxOccurrences.what: a restrictedImports() call that names no RUNTIME_PATHS (the canonical config has the two restrictedImports({}) calls, the Node-code block and the root-entry block, which names VENDOR_SDK_PATHS)
maxOccurrences.fix: Name RUNTIME_PATHS: restrictedImports({ paths: without(RUNTIME_PATHS, ONE_EXEMPTED_ENTRY), patterns: [NODE_BUILTINS] }); a call without it drops every vendor, Text, react-intl and memo ban for its files.
Delete it: the one globalIgnores list holds the generated and agent folders plus ...PRE_EXISTING.

maxOccurrences.what: an ignores key (the canonical config has two: tests out of the zones block, tests out of the FormatJS block; a block with only ignores is a global ignore)
maxOccurrences.fix: Delete it: a block-level ignores list takes those files out of the block's rules, and a block with only ignores hides the files from every rule.

structure.$comment: check-configs compares eslint.config.mjs with the skill's own templates/eslint.config.mjs: every canonical block (files, ignores, rules, extends, options) present, unchanged and in order; every other block names exact files; every file group keeps its canonical globs; every other top-level const is verbatim. wideningGroups may gain any glob (their blocks add bans); the other file groups gain only exact file names. knobs are the consts an app fills (PRE_EXISTING, the multi-package switch and its import pattern). supersets may gain entries but never lose one (a new vendor SDK, a new banned package).

appScope.$comment: Top-level names that always hold app code, next to the layout folders (srcDir, routesDir, testDir, mocksDir, scriptsDir), the workspaces and layoutEntries. No ignore list may reach into them.
